questions.statement: Which word in English describes the weather when the sky is full of clouds and you cannot see the sun?
questions.context: In a classroom in Bogota, a teacher shows pictures of the sky: sunny, rainy, cloudy, and windy.

options.text: Cloudy.
options.feedback: "Cloudy" describes a sky covered with clouds, so the sun is hidden.

options.text: Sunny.
options.feedback: "Sunny" means the sun is bright and there are few or no clouds.

options.text: Windy.
options.feedback: "Windy" describes moving air, not a sky full of clouds.

options.text: Rainy.
options.feedback: "Rainy" describes falling water, not just clouds covering the sun.

questions.explanation: Recognizing basic weather words in English by matching each word with the sky condition it describes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why do people in Cartagena wear light clothes?
questions.context: Read: "Cartagena is very hot and sunny almost all year, so people go to the beach and wear light clothes."

options.text: Because the weather there is hot and sunny.
options.feedback: The text connects hot and sunny weather with wearing light clothes.

options.text: Because it is very cold and snowy every day.
options.feedback: The text says Cartagena is hot, not cold or snowy.

options.text: Because it rains heavily every single hour.
options.feedback: Constant heavy rain is not mentioned in the text.

options.text: Because the city is high in the snowy mountains.
options.feedback: Cartagena is on the coast, and the text does not mention mountains.

questions.explanation: Understanding a cause-effect relationship about weather in a short descriptive text in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the present continuous to describe the weather at this moment?
questions.context: A student in Medellin looks out of the window and says: "It is raining now. I need an umbrella."

options.text: It is raining right now.
options.feedback: "Is raining" is the correct present continuous form to describe weather happening now.

options.text: It rain right now.
options.feedback: "Rain" without "is" and "-ing" is not the present continuous form.

options.text: It raining right now.
options.feedback: "Raining" needs the auxiliary "is" to form the present continuous.

options.text: It rains right now.
options.feedback: The simple present "rains" is used for routines, not for what is happening at this moment.

questions.explanation: Applying the present continuous with weather expressions to describe what is happening at the moment of speaking.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word correctly completes the sentence about the seasons in Colombia?
questions.context: A teacher in Cali writes on the board: "In Colombia we have two main seasons: the dry season and the ______ season."

options.text: Rainy.
options.feedback: In Colombia the two main seasons are the dry season and the rainy season.

options.text: Snowy.
options.feedback: Snow is not a main season in most of Colombia; the opposite of dry is rainy.

options.text: Foggy.
options.feedback: Fog is a weather condition, not the name of the second main season.

options.text: Windy.
options.feedback: Windy days happen, but the standard pair is dry season and rainy season.

questions.explanation: Completing sentences about Colombian seasons using the correct weather vocabulary in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the word "windy" correctly to describe Barranquilla?
questions.context: Ana lives in Barranquilla, a coastal city where it is hot and the air often moves strongly.

options.text: It is windy in Barranquilla, so the flags move a lot.
options.feedback: In a windy place, moving air makes flags and kites move.

options.text: It is windy in Barranquilla, so the sun does not exist.
options.feedback: Wind does not make the sun disappear; that is not what "windy" means.

options.text: It is windy in Barranquilla, so the city is always cold and snowy.
options.feedback: Wind does not mean cold and snowy; Barranquilla is described as hot.

options.text: It is windy in Barranquilla, so people never go outside.
options.feedback: People can go outside on windy days; this does not explain the word "windy".

questions.explanation: Using the weather adjective "windy" in a meaningful sentence about a real Colombian city.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which comparison correctly explains why the weather in Bogota and Cartagena is different?
questions.context: Read: "Bogota is cold and cloudy because it is high in the mountains. Cartagena is hot and sunny because it is on the Caribbean coast."

options.text: Bogota is cold because of its high altitude, while Cartagena is hot because it is on the coast.
options.feedback: The text links Bogota's cold weather to height and Cartagena's heat to its coastal location.

options.text: Both cities have exactly the same weather all year.
options.feedback: The text describes different weather in each city, so they are not the same.

options.text: Cartagena is cold because it is high in the mountains.
options.feedback: The text places Cartagena on the coast, not in the mountains.

options.text: Bogota is hot because it is next to the sea.
options.feedback: The text says Bogota is cold and in the mountains, not next to the sea.

questions.explanation: Comparing two cities to explain how location and altitude affect weather in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: On which day should a student take an umbrella to school?
questions.context: Read a short weather report: "On Monday it is sunny in Cali. On Tuesday it is rainy and cloudy. On Wednesday it is windy and cool."

options.text: Tuesday, because it is rainy and cloudy.
options.feedback: An umbrella is useful on a rainy day, and Tuesday is described as rainy.

options.text: Monday, because it is sunny.
options.feedback: During sunny weather an umbrella is not needed for rain.

options.text: Wednesday, because it is windy.
options.feedback: Wind alone does not require an umbrella for rain.

options.text: No day, because it never rains in Cali.
options.feedback: The report clearly says it is rainy on Tuesday.

questions.explanation: Analyzing a simple weather report to decide which item is needed on a specific day.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the most important message of this paragraph?
questions.context: Read: "Colombia has different climate zones: hot on the coasts, mild in the coffee region, and cold in the high mountains. People wear different clothes in each zone."

options.text: Colombia has different climate zones, so people wear different clothes in each one.
options.feedback: The paragraph links the variety of climate zones with the different clothes people wear.

options.text: All of Colombia is equally hot and sunny every day.
options.feedback: The text describes hot, mild, and cold zones, so the country is not equally hot everywhere.

options.text: People in Colombia always wear the same clothes in every zone.
options.feedback: The text says the opposite: clothing changes from zone to zone.

options.text: The coasts of Colombia are the coldest places in the country.
options.feedback: The text describes the coasts as hot and the mountains as cold.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main message of a short expository paragraph about Colombian climate zones.
questions.subject: ingles
